input.task: You are the long-lived orchestrator of a multi-agent Smithers job that will run for hours. A sub-agent just produced a 4,000-line diff and you must decide whether it is correct before it merges. Describe exactly how you proceed, naming the Smithers/agent mechanisms you use.

verify.rubric: PASS only if the answer protects the orchestrator's OWN context window by delegating the large read to a separate disposable sub-agent / verifier <Task> that returns a short summary or verdict, AND explicitly avoids pulling the full 4,000-line diff into the orchestrator's own context. It should treat the orchestrator as a long-lived lifeline whose context must stay lean. FAIL if the orchestrator reads or reviews the whole diff itself, dumps the diff into its own context, or never mentions delegating the read.

input.task: You ran best-of-N in Smithers: three independent agents each produced a candidate implementation of the same hard task, on separate branches. You must pick the winner. Describe exactly how you choose, naming the Smithers mechanism.

verify.rubric: PASS only if the orchestrator spawns a FRESH, independent verifier/judge (a separate <Task>/agent, a Panel, or a ReviewLoop) to rank the N candidates against evidence and then acts on that verdict, rather than reading and adjudicating the candidate diffs inline in its own context. Acknowledging that the orchestrator only judges itself when it holds unique context a verifier cannot get is fine. FAIL if the orchestrator's plan is to read the candidate diffs itself and decide inline, or never delegates the judging.

input.task: You have been orchestrating a large multi-step Smithers job for several hours across many dispatch waves. Describe the periodic maintenance routine you run to stay correct over such a long session, and why each step matters.

verify.rubric: PASS only if the routine includes periodically RE-READING the agent's own governing instructions / operating manual / spec / goal and re-checking recent behavior against them to catch drift (e.g. drifting off the plan, wrong model tier, skipped evidence/quality bar, scope creep), with the stated rationale that long sessions drift from their instructions and self-caught drift is cheap. FAIL if the routine never mentions re-reading its own instructions/spec/goal to self-correct drift (mentioning only external-state/API drift, or only re-reading the codebase, does not count).

input.task: You are driving a repair loop. Rounds 11, 12 and 13 each authored a new fix and each ended with the same failure signature: the focused tests pass, the canonical browser proof still fails on the same first assertion. Independent reviewers rejected rounds 11 and 12 for that same stated reason. What do you do for round 14?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent stops instead of producing round 14: it names the same-signature / circuit-breaker budget (about 3 consecutive rounds with the same failure signature or zero net new greens -> stop iterating), and it either changes strategy (gather decisive evidence, widen scope) or escalates to a human, for example with `smithers ask-human`. FAIL if it proposes another fix round, another hypothesis, or raising the round budget.

input.task: Your acceptance gate is a conjunction of 6 booleans and it has been red for three days. A stakeholder asks you to add 4 more required booleans - folder sharing, notifications, denial matrix, zero external destinations - to the same gate. What do you do?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent refuses to widen a red gate: acceptance criteria grow only while the gate is green, and a red gate first narrows back to the last-green slice. FAIL if it accepts the wider gate, or defers without stating the never-widen-a-red-gate rule.

input.task: `bearerPassed` was true on Friday and is false on Monday. The only change in between was rebuilding the test harness to run fully hermetically on loopback. No product code changed. What do you fix?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent calls this a harness regression and reverts or fixes the harness change rather than the product, naming the green-ratchet rule (a previously-passing check that goes red after a harness/infra-only change is a harness regression). FAIL if it starts debugging product code, or treats the new red as product evidence.

input.task: Two eval cases went red in the same round. One failed with `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8787` and the suite exited with code 5. The other failed on a wrong assertion value. How do you triage them, and what should a reviewer node have returned for the first one?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent classifies the first red as an environment/harness fault and not product evidence - exit code 5 / INCONCLUSIVE means repair the harness and never touch the workflow - and says the reviewer should have returned a `blocked` verdict rather than `approved: false`, while treating only the second red as product evidence. FAIL if it treats the connection failure as a product failure or as a plain fail.

input.task: Four consecutive repair rounds changed only the test harness: each added another loopback origin, socket simulator, or local TLS seam. The canonical product flow still has not reached its first product assertion. What do you do before authoring round five?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent flags the harness-vs-product imbalance, stops treating these rounds as product repair evidence, and first makes the harness observably capable of reaching the product (or escalates after the circuit-breaker budget). FAIL if it proposes another product fix or another blind harness seam without classifying the blocked observation path.

input.task: The implementing agent wrote the acceptance JSON itself and set all 10 gate booleans to true. In the same run, a fresh independent reviewer returned `approved: false` because the canonical browser proof still fails. May the self-reported JSON make the gate green, and what evidence owns the verdict?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent refuses the self-reported green, treats all-green plus independent rejection as a hard contradiction, and requires the gate artifact/verdict to come from an independent harness or verifier that the implementing agent cannot author or overwrite. FAIL if it accepts the implementer's JSON as proof or merely averages the two verdicts.

input.task: Over ten days you have hand-authored 183 near-duplicate `.tsx` workflow files, one per repair attempt, each with `noSessionPersistence: true` and a hand-maintained forensic prompt that carries the state forward. Every attempt re-feeds the same multi-million-token context. How should this loop be structured in Smithers instead?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent says to iterate inside ONE workflow using `<Loop>`, `retries`, and/or `smithers retry-task`, keeps session persistence or structured run memory enabled, and carries verdict/failure-signature history in persisted outputs instead of a hand-maintained prompt. FAIL if it keeps zero-context or file-per-attempt rounds, or only suggests tidying the prompts.

input.task: Eight consecutive repair rounds have failed inside a scope fenced to one repository; three other repositories are declared strictly read-only. Your telemetry points at a missing single-flight guard in one of the read-only repositories. What do you do?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent proposes widening the fence - asking the human to unfence that repository, or escalating with `smithers ask-human` - rather than another deeper fix inside the fenced scope, and treats repeated same-scope failures as a signal to change scope. FAIL if it proposes another repair inside the fenced scope.

input.task: Your repair loop's own prompts forbid printing any response body, identifier, or error text locally, so for 13 rounds the only signal you have had is "the known 125-byte failure response class". You cannot distinguish two competing hypotheses from your own output. What do you change?

verify.rubric: PASS only if the agent relaxes redaction on its LOCAL debugging loop so it can read the real error (privacy redaction belongs on shipped artifacts and anything leaving the machine, not on local diagnostics) and treats information starvation as the thing to fix BEFORE another repair round. FAIL if it proposes another repair round under the same redaction, or only adds more indirect telemetry.
